findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for each employee were not available during the inspection. The person-in-charge (PIC) stated that employees will sign the forms when the owner is available at the facility. The inspector offered to provide blank copies for the facility to complete. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site. The inspector will follow up on 02/17/2026 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [PF]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The sanitizer test strips at the facility were observed to be wet and unusable. The PIC stated the test strips were accidentally dropped in water over the weekend and new test strips have been ordered. Ensure sanitizer test strips are available and usable at the facility at all times. The inspector will follow up on 02/17/2026 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [PF]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to have accumulations of dust and soil:

1. FIRST REPEAT - Dust accumulation was observed on the fan guard in the walk-in cooler.
2. Debris accumulation was observed on the walk-in cooler floor, especially under the food shelving.
3. Debris accumulation was observed in the corner area near the thermostats under the pizza oven.
4. Soil accumulation was observed on the food shelving in the walk-in cooler.
5. Food debris accumulation was observed inside the utensil holder container located by the three-compartment sink.
6. Food debris accumulation was observed inside the container used to store pizza cutters for customers at the server station.
7. Food debris accumulation was observed on the top surface of the oven. 
8. FIRST REPEAT - Soil accumulation was observed on the inside of the ice machine baffles.
9. Soil accumulation was observed on the soda gun holster.

The PIC was informed of the above conditions and instructed to clean the listed areas to sight and touch. Ensure all nonfood-contact surfaces are routinely cleaned and maintained free of dust, soil, and food debris accumulation to prevent contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Ice accumulation was observed on the walk-in freezer floor and behind the fan casing. The PIC was informed and instructed to remove the ice buildup to prevent further accumulation. Ensure all ice buildup is cleared and the walk-in freezer is maintained free of ice accumulation by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employee’s failure to use a barrier to shut off the faucet after washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to use a barrier when turning off the faucet after washing their hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Upon arrival and during the inspection, the hand sink was obstructed by a large garbage bin. Discussed with PIC and the bin was removed. Ensure that all hand sinks in the facility are accessible at all times for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil in the baffles of the ice machine. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the baffles of the ice machine will be cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the baffles of the ice machine are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to have an accumulation of dust and soil:
1. the fan guard in the walk-in cooler.
2. the fan guard on the floor in the kitchen.
PIC was made aware of the above mentioned soil accumulations. PIC ensured inspector that the dust accumulation will get clean. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces such as the fan guards mentioned above are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to avoid the contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking on the hand sink in the kitchen area was observed in disrepair. PIC was made aware of the disrepair and PIC ensured inspectors that that the sink will receive the relevant repairs. Ensure that the hand sink is caulk back to the wall to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

findings.comment: An accumulation of ice build up was observed in the walk-in freezer. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the accumulated ice build up will be cleared.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Inspector observed an employee wash hands, use a paper towel as a clean barrier and then proceed to dry hands with the paper towel that was used to turn off the faucet handle which contaminated the towel. The employee was stopped, coached and rewashed hands properly using a clean barrier to turn off the faucet and then a clean towel to dry hands. The violation is considered corrected on site. Train and practice proper hand washing technique.

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Upon arrival the inspector observed a container of frozen soup and a bag of frozen broccoli sitting in the hand sink. The soup and broccoli were moved to the walk in cooler. Never place anything in the hand sink. It shall always remain unobstructed and available for hand washing. The violation is considered corrected on site.

(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Inspector observed approximately seven ounces of turkey, eight ounces of steak and four ounces of chicken to be stored at 45 and above. The turkey was 45F while the chicken and beef were 48F. Boats of chicken and beef stacked 3 high were out of temperature. The turkey was stacked significantly above the fill line of the containers. Store foods properly so that they are held within safe temperatures.  The foods were voluntarily discarded. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

 (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Inspector observed cream in the cooler at bar to be missing a date marking. Cream was discarded. Ensure that items such as cream and milk are properly date marked in all areas of the facility. The cream was discarded as they were unsure as to when it was opened. Practice proper date marking. The complaint is considered corrected on site. 

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

Inspector observed glasses with straws and no lids on the counter in the kitchen that staff was using to drink from. Containers were discarded and replaced with cups that had lids and straws. Take care to use proper containers for drinking.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Inspector observed 6 bags of ice on the floor of the walk in freezer. Bags of ice were discarded. Properly protect food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Hard cooked eggs in the prep top have an internal temperature of  54F. Eight eggs were discarded. Eggs deeper in the pan were kept as their internal temperature was 40F.  Take care to fill pans to the fill line and not over. Eggs were stacked high up out of the cooling area of the unit. The was corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The sandwich make table L is holding food at 45F. The temperature log shows that the temperatures this morning (11am) were between 38F and 41F. Refrigeration repair company was called and they will be out to evaluate the unit today. The lack of rails and dented lid (both of which are on order) is exacerbating the issue. The food was moved to the walk in cooler. If they get busy, small portions will be taken out and used with time as a control. Place time on the foods that are held in the unit and use or discard in 4 hours. A follow up will be conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The caulk seal at the three part sink is soiled. Maintain the seal clean, and in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to improperly wash hands - no barrier was used to turn off the faucets after appropriate handwashing. Discussed with PIC and employee. Ensure a barrier such as a paper towel is utilized to turn off the faucet after washing hands - prevent cross contamination. COS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed a quaternary ammonium spray bottle to be used with rags. Cease practice. Facility should either utilize paper towels with the spray bottle and dispose of the paper towels after use or utilize a rag that is stored in quat sanitizer solution in-between uses. Discussed with PIC and employee. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

Observed a stack of cups at the bar to be stacked wet - no air drying before stacking. Cease practice. Ensure cups are air dried before stacking. Discussed with PIC and employee.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non food-contact surfaces to be in need of cleaning:
1. Spray nozzle of the 3 compartment sink in the kitchen had mold and food debris underneath the nozzle. Ensure employees clean the underside and spray squeezer area of the spray nozzle as needed to prevent debris build-up. Discussed with PIC.
2. Walk-in cooler fan has accumulation of dust. Ensure the walk-in cooler fans are washed, rinsed, and sanitized to avoid dust accumulation. Clean as needed to prevent.

Ensure areas are cleaned before next routine inspection. Clean as needed to prevent debris and dust build-up.
